body:
You are using regular `` when navigating, which won't resolve correctly. The correct way in your case would be: ```jsx import type { NextPage } from "next" import Link from "next/link" const Home: NextPage = () => { return (
Server side test, should show: /fr/test-cote-serveur/123

Static test, should show: /fr/test-statique/123
) } export default Home ``` https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/next/link `locale="fr"` is only needed if you intend to change the active locale by the way.

@balazsorban44 hey this was not about `<Link>` the `<a>` were in the example by design - I should have provided better reproduction steps but if you run the example repo, and hit the following URL: http://localhost:3000/fr/test-statique/123

You will see the error in the console logs... the links on the homepage were only there to facilitate the testing and `<a>` was used to avoid a client-side page change (basically hitting the URL to reproduce the error on first page load)

@balazsorban44 interesting - I haven't seen any of the [documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/api-reference/data-fetching/get-static-paths) using this. Are you saying you always need to provide the path in `getStaticPaths` ?

In [my current scenario](https://github.com/Avansai/next-multilingual/blob/main/example/next.config.js), the `rewrites` need to be provided in the config so this solution would not work - I guess there is no way to only specify the parameters to get this to work?

@balazsorban44 by the way I did further tests and

```js
params: {
  "test-static": "test-statique",
  id: "123", // This is the default `id` of the test page.
},
locale: "fr",
```

still triggers the warning in the console log, when running `npm run dev`. I've tried a few different things using `npm run build` and `npm run start` - looks like the warning is suppressed but the SSR markup is wrong. It's using the English hydrated path `/test-static/123` for `/fr/test-statique/123` which is not the desired behavior.

When I remove completely `getStaticPaths` and `getStaticProps` the SSR value for `asPath` for `/fr/test-statique/123` is `/test-static/[id]` while the client side value is `/test-statique/123`.

Unless I am wrong should not happen? I thought that `asPath` would always hydrate back the URLs when using query values?

issue.title: `router.asPath` is different in server and in client with rewrites rules

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.body:
### Run `next info` (available from version 12.0.8 and up)
info Operating System: Platform: linux Arch: x64 Version: #1 SMP Wed Oct 28 23:40:43 UTC 2020 Binaries: Node: 16.13.0 npm: 8.4.1 Yarn: N/A pnpm: N/A Relevant packages: next: 12.0.10 react: 17.0.2 react-dom: 17.0.2
### What version of Next.js are you using? 12.0.10 ### What version of Node.js are you using? 16.13.0 ### What browser are you using? Chrome ### What operating system are you using? Ubuntu ### How are you deploying your application? Vercel ### Describe the Bug If a route has a rewrite rule (e.g. `{source: '/blog', destination: '/news'}`), the `router.asPath` property doesn't return the same result in server and in client. This causes problem when using `router.asPath` to [check active link](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/examples/active-class-name/components/ActiveLink.js#L15) for example. ```jsx {link.label} ``` ``` Warning: Prop `className` did not match. Server: "nav_link__PKDMm " Client: "nav_link__PKDMm nav_isActive__gTQA6" ``` I have encountered some more specific cases in the past, this one is the most obvious. But this seems to be a real issue to me or maybe I don't really understand what `rewrites` is for. ### Expected Behavior `router.asPath` should contain the same thing in server-side and in client-side. ### To Reproduce Clone https://github.com/sixclones/nextjs-router-issue ``` npm i npm run dev ``` Open [localhost:3000/blog](http://localhost:3000/blog) and check the console. You should see the mentioned error. Also inside your terminal, you should see ``` Log: -> Nav -> router.asPath /news ``` while on the browser, it displays ``` Log: -> Nav -> router.asPath /blog ``` --- I found several other issues talking about similar subjects but not really clearly, this is why I wanted to address it. Possibly related #32772, #20488, #19574, #21040 & #21565

body: @balazsorban44 I think we should re-open this because this issue was not a documentation problem.

@nbouvrette this behavior seems expected, you are rewriting to a static path which is prerendered so the `asPath` won't be updated until on the client. See related documentation around the `asPath` caveat added in https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/36876
